title.zh: 卷一百二十二 列傳第十 郭子興 韓林兒
title.raw: 卷一百二十二 列傳第十 郭子興 韓林兒 Volume 122 Biographies 10:

sentences.zh: 郭子興 韓林兒

translations.literal: Guo Zixing; Han Lin'er
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zixing; Han Lin'er

sentences.zh: 郭子興

translations.literal: Guo Zixing
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zixing

sentences.zh: 郭子興，其先曹州人。

translations.literal: Guo Zixing: his ancestors were men of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zixing came of a family originally from Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 父郭公，少以日者術遊定遠，言禍福輒中。

translations.literal: His father, known as Old Guo, in youth practiced the art of the day-calculator and wandered in Dingyuan; when he spoke of fortune and misfortune he was invariably right.
translations.idiomatic: His father, called Old Guo, had traveled Dingyuan in his youth as a diviner, and his predictions of fortune or disaster always proved true.

sentences.zh: 邑富人有瞽女無所歸，郭公乃娶之，家日益饒。

translations.literal: A wealthy man of the district had a blind daughter with nowhere to go; Old Guo then married her, and the household daily grew richer.
translations.idiomatic: A local magnate had a blind daughter with no one to take her in; Old Guo married her, and the family grew steadily wealthier.

sentences.zh: 生三子，子興其仲出。

translations.literal: She bore three sons; Zixing was the second-born.
translations.idiomatic: She bore three sons; Zixing was the middle son.

sentences.zh: 始生，郭公卜之吉。

translations.literal: At his birth Old Guo divined for him and obtained a favorable result.
translations.idiomatic: When he was born, Old Guo cast the lots and received an auspicious omen.

sentences.zh: 及長，任俠，喜賓客。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was chivalrous and fond of guests.
translations.idiomatic: As he came of age he lived by the code of the knight-errant and delighted in entertaining guests.

sentences.zh: 會元政亂，子興散家資，椎牛釃酒，與壯士結納。

translations.literal: It happened that Yuan government was in disorder; Zixing dispersed his family wealth, slaughtered oxen and poured wine, and formed ties with stalwart men.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan rule fell into chaos, Zixing spent down his family fortune, slaughtered cattle and broached wine, and bound himself to bold companions.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年春，集少年數千人，襲據濠州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twelfth year of Zhizheng he gathered several thousand youths and seized Haozhou by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Zhizheng 12 (1352) he rallied several thousand young men and took Haozhou by storm.

sentences.zh: 太祖往從之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor went to enter his service.

sentences.zh: 門者疑其諜，執以告子興。

translations.literal: The gatekeeper suspected him a spy, seized him and reported to Zixing.
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeeper took him for a spy, seized him, and reported to Zixing.

sentences.zh: 子興奇太祖狀貌，解縛與語，收帳下。

translations.literal: Zixing marveled at the Founding Emperor's appearance, loosed his bonds and spoke with him, and took him into his personal following.
translations.idiomatic: Zixing was struck by the Founding Emperor's bearing, had him unbound and talked with him, and enrolled him in his household guard.

sentences.zh: 為十夫長，數從戰有功。

translations.literal: He was made a leader of ten; repeatedly following into battle he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed leader of ten men and repeatedly distinguished himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 子興喜，其次妻小張夫人亦指目太祖曰：「此異人也。

translations.literal: Zixing rejoiced; his second wife, Lady Zhang the Younger, also pointed at the Founding Emperor and said: "This is an extraordinary man."
translations.idiomatic: Zixing was delighted, and his second wife, the younger Lady Zhang, likewise pointed at the Founding Emperor and said, "Here is no ordinary man."

sentences.zh: 」乃妻以所撫馬公女，是為孝慈高皇后。

translations.literal: " He then gave him in marriage the daughter he had raised, the daughter of Lord Ma — this was Empress Xiaoci the High.
translations.idiomatic: " He then gave him in marriage the foster daughter of Lord Ma whom he had raised — she became Empress Xiaoci Gao.

sentences.zh: 始，子興同起事者孫德崖等四人，與子興而五，各稱元帥不相下。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Zixing's fellow risers Sun Deyai and four others, with Zixing making five, each styled themselves marshal and would not yield to one another.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zixing and four others who had risen with him — Sun Deyai among them — made five commanders in all; each called himself marshal and refused to defer to the rest.

sentences.zh: 四人者粗而戇，日剽掠，子興意輕之。

translations.literal: The four were coarse and dull-witted, daily plundering; Zixing in his mind held them light.
translations.idiomatic: The four were crude and rash, looting every day, and Zixing looked down on them.

sentences.zh: 四人不悅，合謀傾子興。

translations.literal: The four were displeased and joined in plot to overthrow Zixing.
translations.idiomatic: The four took offense and conspired together to bring Zixing down.

sentences.zh: 子興以是多家居不視事。

translations.literal: Zixing because of this mostly stayed at home and did not attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Zixing spent much of his time at home and neglected command.

sentences.zh: 太祖乘閑說曰：「彼日益合，我益離，久之必為所制。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, seizing a free moment, urged: "They daily grow more united, we daily more divided; in time we shall certainly be controlled by them."
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor took occasion to warn him: "They grow closer day by day while we drift apart; before long they are sure to have us in their grip."

sentences.zh: 」子興不能從也。

translations.literal: " Zixing could not follow this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: " Zixing would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 元師破徐州，徐帥彭大、趙均用帥餘眾奔濠。

translations.literal: Yuan forces broke Xuzhou; the Xu commander Peng Da and Zhao Junyong led the remaining troops fleeing to Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan troops overran Xuzhou, and the Xu commanders Peng Da and Zhao Junyong led their survivors to Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 德崖等以其故盜魁有名，乃共推奉之，使居己上。

translations.literal: Deyai and the others, because he was a former bandit chieftain of renown, together promoted and honored him, placing him above themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Deyai and his fellows, knowing Peng's fame as a former bandit chief, jointly elevated him and set him above themselves.

sentences.zh: 大有智數，子興與相厚而薄均用。

translations.literal: Peng Da had stratagems and resource; Zixing was thick with him and slighted Junyong.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Da was shrewd and capable; Zixing drew close to him while keeping Junyong at a distance.

sentences.zh: 於是德崖等譖諸均用曰：「子興知有彭將軍耳，不知有將軍也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Deyai and the others slandered Zixing to Junyong, saying: "Zixing knows only General Peng and does not know there is a general [you]."
translations.idiomatic: Deyai and the rest then whispered to Junyong: "Zixing knows only General Peng — he has no regard for you as commander."

sentences.zh: 」均用怒，乘間執子興，幽諸德崖家。

translations.literal: " Junyong was enraged; seizing an opportunity he seized Zixing and confined him in Deyai's house.
translations.idiomatic: " Junyong flew into a rage, seized an opening to arrest Zixing, and shut him up in Deyai's house.

sentences.zh: 太祖自他部歸，大驚，急帥子興二子訴於大。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor returned from another detachment, was greatly alarmed, and hastily led Zixing's two sons to plead before Peng Da.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor came back from another command he was deeply alarmed and at once took Zixing's two sons to appeal to Peng Da.

sentences.zh: 大曰：「吾在，孰敢魚肉而翁者！

translations.literal: Peng Da said: "While I am here, who dares treat your father like fish on the chopping block!"
translations.idiomatic: Peng Da said, "While I stand here, who would dare lay hands on your father as if he were meat on the block!"

sentences.zh: 」與太祖偕詣德崖家，破械出子興，挾之歸。

translations.literal: " He went with the Founding Emperor together to Deyai's house, broke the fetters and brought Zixing out, and escorted him back.
translations.idiomatic: " He went with the Founding Emperor to Deyai's house, broke Zixing's bonds, brought him out, and escorted him home.

sentences.zh: 元師圍濠州，乃釋故憾，共城守五閱月。

translations.literal: Yuan forces besieged Haozhou; they then released old grievances and jointly defended the city for five months.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan troops besieged Haozhou they set aside old grudges and held the city together for five months.

sentences.zh: 圍解，大、均用皆自稱王，而子興及德崖等為元帥如故。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, Da and Junyong each styled themselves king, while Zixing and Deyai and the others remained marshals as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege lifted, Peng Da and Zhao Junyong each proclaimed himself king, while Zixing, Deyai, and the others kept the title of marshal as before.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大死，子早住領其眾。

translations.literal: Before long Peng Da died; his son Zao Zao took command of his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Peng Da died, and his son Zao Zao assumed leadership of his troops.

sentences.zh: 均用專狠益甚，挾子興攻盱眙、泗州，將害之。

translations.literal: Junyong's arbitrary harshness grew worse; he compelled Zixing to attack Xuyi and Sizhou and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Junyong grew ever more domineering and brutal; he forced Zixing to campaign against Xuyi and Sizhou and was on the point of killing him.

sentences.zh: 太祖已取滁，乃遣人說均用曰：「大王窮迫時，郭公開門延納，德至厚也。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor had already taken Chu; he then sent a man to persuade Junyong, saying: "When Your Highness was in desperate straits, Lord Guo opened his gates and received you — his kindness was very great."
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor, having secured Chuzhou, sent someone to reason with Junyong: "When you were hard pressed, Lord Guo welcomed you through his gates — his kindness was profound."

sentences.zh: 大王不能報，反聽細人言圖之，自剪羽翼，失豪傑心，竊為大王不取。

translations.literal: " Your Highness cannot repay this, yet on the contrary heed petty men's words and plot against him — you cut your own wings, lose the hearts of heroes; I privately deem this inadvisable for Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: " Instead of repaying him, you heed petty counsel and plot his ruin — you clip your own wings and forfeit the loyalty of able men; this, I venture, Your Highness should not do."

sentences.zh: 且其部曲猶眾，殺之得無悔乎？

translations.literal: " Moreover his following is still numerous — if you kill him will you not regret it?"
translations.idiomatic: " Besides, his followers are still many — will you not rue killing him?"

sentences.zh: 」均用聞太祖兵甚盛，心憚之，太祖又使人賂其左右，子興用是得免，乃將其所部萬余就太祖于滁。

translations.literal: " Junyong heard the Founding Emperor's troops were very strong and inwardly feared him; the Founding Emperor also sent men to bribe his close attendants — by this Zixing was spared, and then led his division of more than ten thousand to join the Founding Emperor at Chu.
translations.idiomatic: " Junyong, hearing how strong the Founding Emperor's army had become, was afraid; the Founding Emperor also bribed his intimates, and so Zixing escaped harm and brought more than ten thousand of his men to the Founding Emperor at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 子興為人梟悍善鬥，而性悻直少容。

translations.literal: Zixing as a man was fierce and bold, skilled in fighting, yet by nature obstinate and straight, with little forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Zixing was fierce and warlike by nature, yet obstinate and unyielding, with little patience for others.

sentences.zh: 方事急，輒從太祖謀議，親信如左右手。

translations.literal: When affairs were urgent he would follow the Founding Emperor in counsel and planning, trusting him as his own right and left hands.
translations.idiomatic: In a crisis he turned to the Founding Emperor for counsel and trusted him as he would his own hands.

sentences.zh: 事解，即信讒疏太祖。

translations.literal: When the crisis passed he at once believed slander and kept the Founding Emperor at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Once danger had passed he listened to slander and distanced the Founding Emperor.

sentences.zh: 太祖左右任事者悉召之去，稍奪太祖兵柄。

translations.literal: All those around the Founding Emperor who handled affairs he summoned away; he gradually stripped the Founding Emperor of military authority.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled every capable man serving at the Founding Emperor's side and little by little withdrew his command.

sentences.zh: 太祖事子興愈謹。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor served Zixing all the more scrupulously.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor only served Zixing with greater care.

sentences.zh: 將士有所獻，孝慈皇后輒以貽子興妻。

translations.literal: When officers and soldiers had offerings, Empress Xiaoci would at once give them to Zixing's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the troops presented, Empress Xiaoci promptly passed on to Zixing's wife.

sentences.zh: 子興至滁，欲據以自王。

translations.literal: When Zixing reached Chu he wished to hold it and make himself king.
translations.idiomatic: After Zixing came to Chuzhou he meant to seize the place and proclaim himself king.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「滁四面皆山，舟楫商旅不通，非可旦夕安者也。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor said: "Chu on all four sides is ringed by mountains; boats, oars, merchants and travelers do not pass — it is not a place where one can settle in a morning and evening."
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor said, "Chuzhou is walled in by mountains on every side; neither shipping nor trade can pass — it is no seat one can hold for long in comfort."

sentences.zh: 」子興乃已。

translations.literal: " Zixing then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Zixing abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 及取和州，子興命太祖統諸將守其地。

translations.literal: When Hezhou was taken, Zixing ordered the Founding Emperor to command the generals in guarding that territory.
translations.idiomatic: After Hezhou was captured, Zixing put the Founding Emperor in charge of the generals defending the region.

sentences.zh: 德崖饑，就食和境，求駐軍城中，太祖納之。

translations.literal: Deyai was starving; he came to forage in He territory and asked to station troops inside the city — the Founding Emperor admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Deyai, short of provisions, came into Hezhou's borders to forage and asked to quarter his troops in the city; the Founding Emperor allowed it.

sentences.zh: 有讒於子興者。

translations.literal: Someone slandered the Founding Emperor to Zixing.
translations.idiomatic: Someone whispered against the Founding Emperor to Zixing.

sentences.zh: 子興夜至和，太祖來謁，子興怒甚，不與語。

translations.literal: Zixing came by night to He; the Founding Emperor came to pay respects — Zixing was very angry and would not speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zixing arrived at Hezhou by night; when the Founding Emperor came to greet him, Zixing was furious and refused to speak.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「德崖嘗困公，宜為備。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor said: "Deyai once trapped Your Lordship — you should take precautions."
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor said, "Deyai once had you in his power — you ought to stay on guard."

sentences.zh: 」子興默然。

translations.literal: " Zixing was silent.
translations.idiomatic: " Zixing said nothing.

sentences.zh: 德崖聞子興至，謀引去。

translations.literal: Deyai heard Zixing had come and plotted to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When Deyai learned Zixing had arrived, he planned to pull out.

sentences.zh: 前營已發，德崖方留視後軍，而其軍與子興軍鬥，多死者。

translations.literal: The vanguard had already set out; Deyai had only remained to oversee the rear guard, but his army and Zixing's army fought — many died.
translations.idiomatic: The van had already marched off while Deyai stayed behind with the rearguard; his troops then clashed with Zixing's, and many fell on both sides.

sentences.zh: 子興執德崖，太祖亦為德崖軍所執。

translations.literal: Zixing seized Deyai; the Founding Emperor was also seized by Deyai's army.
translations.idiomatic: Zixing took Deyai prisoner, while Deyai's men seized the Founding Emperor in turn.

sentences.zh: 子興聞之，大驚，立遣徐達往代太祖，縱德崖還。

translations.literal: Zixing heard this and was greatly alarmed; he immediately sent Xu Da to replace the Founding Emperor and released Deyai to return.
translations.idiomatic: Zixing was deeply alarmed and at once sent Xu Da to take the Founding Emperor's place, then set Deyai free.

sentences.zh: 德崖軍釋太祖，達亦脫歸。

translations.literal: Deyai's army released the Founding Emperor; Da also escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Deyai's men released the Founding Emperor, and Xu Da likewise made his way back.

sentences.zh: 子興憾德崖甚，將甘心焉，以太祖故強釋之，邑邑不樂。

translations.literal: Zixing resented Deyai deeply and was about to have his heart's satisfaction in killing him; because of the Founding Emperor he forcibly released him, yet was discontented and uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Zixing hated Deyai bitterly and meant to kill him outright, but for the Founding Emperor's sake let him go against his will, brooding all the while.

sentences.zh: 未幾，發病卒，歸葬滁州。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill and died; he was buried back in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill and died, and was buried at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 子興三子。

translations.literal: Zixing had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Zixing had three sons.

sentences.zh: 長子前戰死，次天敘、天爵。

translations.literal: The eldest had died earlier in battle; the next were Tian Xu and Tian Jue.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest had already fallen in battle; the younger sons were Tian Xu and Tian Jue.

sentences.zh: 子興死，韓林兒檄天敘為都元帥，張天祐及太祖副之。

translations.literal: When Zixing died, Han Lin'er issued orders making Tian Xu supreme commander, with Zhang Tianyou and the Founding Emperor as his deputies.
translations.idiomatic: After Zixing's death Han Lin'er appointed Tian Xu supreme commander, with Zhang Tianyou and the Founding Emperor as his lieutenants.

sentences.zh: 天祐，子興婦弟也。

translations.literal: Tianyou was Zixing's wife's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou was the younger brother of Zixing's wife.

sentences.zh: 太祖渡江，天敘、天祐引兵攻集慶，陳野先叛，俱被殺。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor crossed the Yangzi, Tian Xu and Tianyou led troops to attack Jiqing; Chen Yexian rebelled, and both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor crossed the river, Tian Xu and Tianyou marched on Jiqing; Chen Yexian turned traitor, and both were slain.

sentences.zh: 林兒復以天爵為中書右丞。

translations.literal: Lin'er then made Tian Jue Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'er then named Tian Jue Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 已而太祖為平章政事。

translations.literal: Before long the Founding Emperor became Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Founding Emperor was made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天爵失職怨望，久之謀不利於太祖，誅死，子興後遂絕。

translations.literal: Tian Jue, having lost his post, harbored resentment; after a long while he plotted against the Founding Emperor and was executed — Zixing's line then ended.
translations.idiomatic: Deprived of office, Tian Jue nursed a grudge; in time he plotted against the Founding Emperor and was put to death, and Zixing's house came to an end.

sentences.zh: 有一女，小張夫人出者，事太祖為惠妃，生蜀、穀、代三王。

translations.literal: He had one daughter, born of the younger Lady Zhang, who served the Founding Emperor as Consort Hui and bore the three princes of Shu, Gu, and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He also had a daughter by the younger Lady Zhang, who became Consort Hui to the Founding Emperor and bore the Princes of Shu, Gu, and Dai.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年追封子興為滁陽王，詔有司建廟，用中牢祀，復其鄰宥氏，世世守王墓。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Chuyang; an edict ordered the relevant offices to build a temple and sacrifice with the middle offering; his neighbor the You clan was restored, generation after generation to guard the prince's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 (1370) Zixing was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Chuyang; the throne ordered officials to raise a temple and offer the middle sacrifice, restored the neighboring You clan, and charged them to guard the royal tomb in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 十六年，太祖手書子興事蹟，命太常丞張來儀文其碑。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the Founding Emperor in his own hand wrote Zixing's deeds and ordered Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Laiyi to compose the text for his stele.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the Founding Emperor wrote out Zixing's career in his own hand and charged Vice Director of Sacrifices Zhang Laiyi with the stele inscription.

sentences.zh: 滁人郭老舍者，宣德中以滁陽王親，朝京師。

translations.literal: A man of Chu named Old Guo She, in the Xuande reign claimed kinship with the Prince of Chuyang and came to court in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Xuande a Chu native named Guo She claimed descent from the Prince of Chuyang and presented himself at court.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，有郭琥自言四世祖老舍，滁陽王第四子，予冠帶奉祀。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi reign a Guo Hu claimed that his fourth-generation ancestor was Old Guo She, fourth son of the Prince of Chuyang, and was granted cap and girdle to perform sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi, one Guo Hu asserted that his fourth-generation forebear Guo She was the prince's fourth son; he was given official rank to conduct the rites.

sentences.zh: 已，為宥氏所訐。

translations.literal: Afterward he was impeached by the You clan.
translations.idiomatic: Later the You clan brought charges against him.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「滁陽王祀典，太祖所定，曰無後，廟碑昭然，老舍非滁陽王子。

translations.literal: The ritual officials said: "The sacrificial regulations for the Prince of Chuyang were fixed by the Founding Emperor, stating he had no posterity; temple and stele make this clear — Old Guo She was not a son of the Prince of Chuyang."
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Rites reported: "The Founding Emperor himself fixed the Chuyang cult and declared the line extinct; temple and stele say so plainly — Guo She was no son of the prince."

sentences.zh: 」奪奉祀。

translations.literal: " His right to sacrifice was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: " His privilege to officiate was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 韓林兒

translations.literal: Han Lin'er
translations.idiomatic: Han Lin'er

sentences.zh: 韓林兒，欒城人，或言李氏子也。

translations.literal: Han Lin'er was a man of Luancheng; some say he was a son of the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lin'er came from Luancheng; some held that he was in fact a Li by birth.

sentences.zh: 其先世以白蓮會燒香惑眾，謫徙永年。

translations.literal: His forebears, through the White Lotus Society burning incense to delude the masses, were banished and relocated to Yongnian.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had led the White Lotus Society in incense rites to sway the people and were exiled to Yongnian.

sentences.zh: 元末，林兒父山童鼓妖言，謂「天下當大亂，彌勒佛下生」。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan, Lin'er's father Mountain Boy beat demonic talk, saying "The realm is about to fall into great disorder; Maitreya Buddha is descending to be born."
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yuan, Lin'er's father Han Shantong spread prophecy that the world would soon be in chaos and Maitreya would descend to earth.

sentences.zh: 河南、江、淮間愚民多信之。

translations.literal: Among the foolish folk between Henan and the Yangzi and Huai many believed this.
translations.idiomatic: Simple folk across Henan and the Yangzi–Huai region largely believed him.

sentences.zh: 潁州人劉福通與其党杜遵道、羅文素、盛文鬱等復言「山童，宋徽宗八世孫，當主中國」。

translations.literal: Liu Futong of Yingzhou and his partisans Du Zundao, Luo Wensu, Sheng Wenyu and others again declared: "Mountain Boy is the eighth-generation descendant of Emperor Huizong of Song and ought to rule China."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Futong of Yingzhou and his fellows Du Zundao, Luo Wensu, and Sheng Wenyu proclaimed that Shantong was the eighth-generation descendant of Song Huizong and destined to rule China.

sentences.zh: 乃殺白馬黑牛，誓告天地，謀起兵，以紅巾為號。

translations.literal: They then killed a white horse and black ox, swore before Heaven and Earth, plotted to raise troops, and took the red turban as their sign.
translations.idiomatic: They sacrificed a white horse and a black ox, swore their oath to Heaven and Earth, planned rebellion, and took the red turban as their banner.

sentences.zh: 至正十一年五月，事覺，福通等遽入潁州反，而山童為吏所捕誅。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year of Zhizheng the affair was discovered; Futong and the others hastily entered Yingzhou in revolt, while Mountain Boy was seized by officials and executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Zhizheng 11 (1351) the plot was exposed; Futong and his men at once rose in Yingzhou, while Shantong was arrested and executed.

sentences.zh: 林兒與母楊氏逃武安山中。

translations.literal: Lin'er and his mother, née Yang, fled into the mountains of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'er and his mother Lady Yang fled into the Wu'an hills.

sentences.zh: 福通據硃皋，破羅山、上蔡、真陽、確山，犯葉、舞陽，陷汝寧、光、息，眾至十余萬，元兵不能禦。

translations.literal: Futong held Zhugao, broke Luoshan, Shangcai, Zhenyang, Queshan, struck Ye and Wuyang, took Runing, Guang, and Xi — his host reached more than a hundred thousand, and Yuan troops could not withstand him.
translations.idiomatic: Futong seized Zhugao, overran Luoshan, Shangcai, Zhenyang, and Queshan, raided Ye and Wuyang, and captured Runing, Guang, and Xi; his forces swelled past a hundred thousand, and Yuan armies could not check them.

sentences.zh: 時徐壽輝等起蘄、黃，布王三、孟海馬等起湘、漢，芝麻李起豐、沛，而郭子興亦據濠應之。

translations.literal: At this time Xu Shouhui and others rose in Qian and Huang; Bu Wangsan, Meng Haima and others rose in Xiang and Han; Sesame Li rose in Feng and Pei — and Guo Zixing also held Hao in response.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Xu Shouhui rose in Qizhou and Huangzhou, Bu Wangsan and Meng Haima in Hunan and Hubei, Sesame Li in Feng and Pei, and Guo Zixing seized Haozhou in the same cause.

sentences.zh: 時皆謂之「紅軍」，亦稱「香軍」。

translations.literal: At the time all called them the "Red Army," also styled the "Fragrant Army."
translations.idiomatic: People called them the Red Army, or sometimes the Fragrant Army.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月，福通物色林兒，得諸碭山夾河；

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year Futong sought out Lin'er and found him between Dangshan and the Jia River;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifteenth year Futong tracked Lin'er down between Dangshan and the Jia River;

sentences.zh: 迎至亳，僭稱皇帝，又號小明王，建國曰宋，建元龍鳳。

translations.literal: welcomed him to Bo, presumptuously styled him emperor, also titled him Lesser Ming King, founded a state called Song, and established the era Longfeng.
translations.idiomatic: brought him to Bo, had him proclaimed emperor and styled Lesser Ming King, revived the name Song for his state, and adopted the reign title Longfeng.

sentences.zh: 拆鹿邑太清宮材，治宮闕於亳。

translations.literal: They dismantled timber from the Supreme Clarity Palace of Luyi to build palaces at Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Timber from the Supreme Clarity Palace at Luyi was torn out to erect palaces at Bo.

sentences.zh: 尊楊氏為皇太后，遵道、文郁為丞相，福通、文素平章政事，劉六知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Lady Yang was honored as Empress Dowager; Zundao and Wenyu were made Chancellors; Futong and Wensu were Directors of the Secretariat; Liu Liu directed the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang was made Empress Dowager; Du Zundao and Sheng Wenyu became chancellors; Liu Futong and Luo Wensu directors of the secretariat; Liu Liu headed military affairs.

sentences.zh: 劉六者，福通弟也。

translations.literal: Liu Liu was Futong's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liu was Futong's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 遵道寵用事。

translations.literal: Zundao, favored, monopolized power.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zundao, in favor, held real power.

sentences.zh: 福通嫉之，陰命甲士撾殺遵道，自為丞相，加太保，事權一歸福通。

translations.literal: Futong envied him; secretly he ordered armored soldiers to beat Zundao to death, made himself Chancellor, added Grand Guardian — all authority returned to Futong alone.
translations.idiomatic: Futong, jealous, secretly had armed men beat Du Zundao to death, took the chancellorship himself with the title Grand Guardian, and concentrated every lever of power in his own hands.

sentences.zh: 既而元師大敗福通于太康，進圍亳，福通挾林兒走安豐。

translations.literal: Before long Yuan forces greatly defeated Futong at Taikang and advanced to besiege Bo; Futong, taking Lin'er with him, fled to Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuan troops routed Futong at Taikang and pressed the siege of Bo; Futong fled with Lin'er to Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 未幾，兵復盛，遣其黨分道略地。

translations.literal: Before long their armies flourished again; he sent his partisans by separate routes to seize territory.
translations.idiomatic: Before long their forces revived; he sent his lieutenants out on separate paths to overrun the land.

sentences.zh: 十七年，李武、崔德陷商州，遂破武關以圖關中，而毛貴陷膠、萊、益都、濱州，山東郡邑多下。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Li Wu and Cui De took Shangzhou, then broke Wuguan to aim at Guanzhong, while Mao Gui took Jiao, Lai, Yidu, and Binzhou — many commanderies and districts of Shandong fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Li Wu and Cui De captured Shangzhou, broke through Wuguan toward Guanzhong, while Mao Gui overran Jiao, Lai, Yidu, and Binzhou; most of Shandong's prefectures submitted.

sentences.zh: 是年六月，福通帥眾攻汴梁，且分軍三道：關先生、破頭潘、馮長舅、沙劉二、王士誠趨晉、冀；

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year Futong led the host to attack Bianliang and moreover divided the army into three routes: Master Guan, Broken-head Pan, Feng the Long Maternal Uncle, Sha Liu the Second, and Wang Shicheng pressed toward Jin and Ji;
translations.idiomatic: That June Futong marched on Kaifeng and split his army three ways: Master Guan, Broken-head Pan, Feng the Long Uncle, Sha Liu the Second, and Wang Shicheng drove into Shanxi and Hebei;

sentences.zh: 白不信、大刀敖、李喜喜趨關中；

translations.literal: Bai Buxin, Great-blade Ao, and Li Xixi pressed toward Guanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: Bai Buxin, Great-blade Ao, and Li Xixi pushed into Guanzhong;

sentences.zh: 毛貴出山東北犯。

translations.literal: Mao Gui came out from Shandong and invaded northeastward.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Gui marched out of Shandong and struck northward.

sentences.zh: 勢銳甚。

translations.literal: Their momentum was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Their advance was fierce.

sentences.zh: 田豐者，元鎮守黃河義兵萬戶也，叛附福通，陷濟寧，尋敗走。

translations.literal: Tian Feng was a Yuan defender of the Yellow River, a militia commander of ten thousand households; he rebelled and joined Futong, took Jining, and soon was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Feng had been a Yuan commander of Yellow River militia with a ten-thousand-household warrant; he defected to Futong, captured Jining, but was soon routed and driven off.

sentences.zh: 其秋，福通兵陷大名，遂自曹、濮陷衛輝。

translations.literal: That autumn Futong's army took Daming, then from Cao and Pu took Weihui.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Futong's forces seized Daming and, pushing from Cao and Pu, overran Weihui.

sentences.zh: 白不信、大刀敖、李喜喜陷興元，遂入鳳翔，屢為察罕帖木兒、李思齊所破，走入蜀。

translations.literal: Bai Buxin, Great-blade Ao, and Li Xixi took Xingyuan, then entered Fengxiang; repeatedly they were broken by Chaghan Temür and Li Sizhi, and fled into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Buxin, Great-blade Ao, and Li Xixi captured Xingyuan and advanced into Fengxiang, but Chaghan Temür and Li Sizhi defeated them again and again until they fled into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十八年，田豐復陷東平、濟寧、東昌、益都、廣平、順德。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Tian Feng again took Dongping, Jining, Dongchang, Yidu, Guangping, and Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Tian Feng recaptured Dongping, Jining, Dongchang, Yidu, Guangping, and Shunde.

sentences.zh: 毛貴亦數敗元兵，陷清、滄，據長蘆鎮，尋陷濟南；

translations.literal: Mao Gui also repeatedly defeated Yuan troops, took Qing and Cang, held Changlu Town, and soon took Jinan;
translations.idiomatic: Mao Gui likewise defeated Yuan forces several times, seized Qing and Cang, held Changlu, and soon captured Jinan;

sentences.zh: 益引兵北，殺宣慰使董搏霄于南皮，陷薊州，犯漷州，略柳林以逼大都。

translations.literal: further leading troops north, he killed Pacification Commissioner Dong Boxiao at Nanpi, took Jizhou, struck Huazhou, raided Liulin to press upon Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: then pressed farther north, killed Pacification Commissioner Dong Boxiao at Nanpi, took Jizhou, threatened Huazhou, and swept Liulin to menace Dadu.

sentences.zh: 順帝征四方兵入衛，議欲遷都避其鋒，大臣諫乃止。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun summoned troops from the four quarters to guard the capital; there was discussion of moving the capital to avoid their edge — ministers remonstrated and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun called in armies from every quarter to defend the capital; courtiers debated shifting the capital to escape the rebels, but senior ministers dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 貴旋被元兵擊敗，還據濟南。

translations.literal: Gui was soon defeated by Yuan troops and returned to hold Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was soon beaten back by Yuan forces and fell back on Jinan.

sentences.zh: 而福通出沒河南北，五月攻下汴梁，守將竹貞遁去，遂迎林兒都焉。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Futong ranged north and south of the Yellow River; in the fifth month he attacked and took Bianliang — the defending general Zhu Zhen fled — and then welcomed Lin'er to make it his capital.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Futong ranged across the Henan region; in the fifth month he stormed Kaifeng, its defender Zhu Zhen fled, and he installed Lin'er as his court there.

sentences.zh: 關先生、破頭潘等又分其軍為二，一出絳州，一出沁州。

translations.literal: Master Guan, Broken-head Pan and others again divided their army in two — one column out from Jiangzhou, one out from Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Master Guan, Broken-head Pan, and the rest split their forces again, one column from Jiangzhou and one from Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾太行，破遼、潞，遂陷冀寧；

translations.literal: They crossed the Taihang, broke Liao and Lu, and then took Jining;
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Taihang range, overran Liao and Lu, and seized Jining;

sentences.zh: 攻保定不克，陷完州，掠大同、興和塞外諸郡，至陷上都，毀諸宮殿，轉掠遼陽，抵高麗。

translations.literal: they attacked Baoding without success, took Wanzhou, plundered Datong, Xinghe and the outer prefectures beyond the passes, even took Shangdu and destroyed the palaces, turned to raid Liaoyang, and reached Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: failed at Baoding but took Wanzhou, ravaged Datong, Xinghe, and the frontier prefectures, sacked Shangdu and razed its palaces, swept through Liaoyang, and pushed as far as Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 十九年陷遼陽，殺懿州路總管呂震。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year they took Liaoyang and killed Yizhou Circuit Administrator Lü Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year they captured Liaoyang and killed Yizhou circuit intendant Lü Zhen.

sentences.zh: 順帝以上都宮闕盡廢，自此不復北巡。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun, because the palaces of Shangdu were wholly ruined, from this time no longer made northern tours.
translations.idiomatic: With Shangdu's palaces in ruins, Emperor Shun never toured the north again.

sentences.zh: 李喜喜餘黨復陷寧夏，略靈武諸邊地。

translations.literal: The remnant band of Li Xixi again took Ningxia and overran the borderlands of Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xixi's surviving followers seized Ningxia again and raided the Lingwu frontier.

sentences.zh: 是時承平久，川郡皆無守備。

translations.literal: At this time long peace had prevailed; riverine prefectures all lacked defenses.
translations.idiomatic: After long peace the inland prefectures had no defenses worth the name.

sentences.zh: 長吏聞賊來，輒棄城遁，以故所至無不摧破。

translations.literal: When senior officials heard bandits were coming they at once abandoned cities and fled — for this reason wherever the rebels went nothing failed to be smashed.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials fled at the first rumor of rebels, so every place they touched collapsed without resistance.

sentences.zh: 然林兒本起盜賊，無大志，又聽命福通，徒擁虛名。

translations.literal: Yet Lin'er had risen from banditry and had no great ambition; he moreover obeyed Futong's orders and merely held an empty name.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lin'er was a bandit chieftain at heart, without grand ambition, and took orders from Futong — a king in name only.

sentences.zh: 諸將在外者率不遵約束，所過焚劫，至啖老弱為糧，且皆福通故等夷，福通亦不能制。

translations.literal: The generals abroad mostly did not obey discipline; wherever they passed they burned and plundered, even eating the old and weak for provisions — and all were Futong's former equals; Futong also could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Field commanders routinely ignored orders, burning and looting wherever they marched, even feeding on the old and weak; they had been Futong's peers, and he could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 兵雖盛，威令不行。

translations.literal: Though their troops were numerous, authority and orders did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: For all their numbers, command meant nothing.

sentences.zh: 數攻下城邑，元兵亦數從其後復之，不能守。

translations.literal: Repeatedly they attacked and took cities and towns; Yuan troops also repeatedly recovered them from behind — they could not hold them.
translations.idiomatic: They seized town after town, only to lose them as Yuan forces retook them from the rear.

sentences.zh: 惟毛貴稍有智略。

translations.literal: Only Mao Gui had a little strategy and resource.
translations.idiomatic: Only Mao Gui showed any real planning.

sentences.zh: 其破濟南也，立賓興院，選用元故官姬宗周等分守諸路。

translations.literal: When he took Jinan he established a Guest-Exaltation Academy and selected former Yuan officials such as Ji Zongzhou to divide and guard the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After capturing Jinan he set up a civil-service academy and appointed former Yuan officials such as Ji Zongzhou to govern the circuits.

sentences.zh: 又於萊州立屯田三百六十所，每屯相距三十里，造挽運大車百輛，凡官民田十取其二。

translations.literal: He also at Lai established three hundred sixty military colonies, each colony thirty li apart, built one hundred large transport wagons — from official and private fields alike he took two parts in ten.
translations.idiomatic: At Lai he founded three hundred sixty garrison farms thirty li apart, built a hundred heavy transport carts, and levied a tithe of two parts in ten on public and private land alike.

sentences.zh: 多所規畫，故得據山東者三年。

translations.literal: He made many plans and regulations; therefore he was able to hold Shandong for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Such measures let him hold Shandong for three years.

sentences.zh: 及察罕帖木兒數破賊，盡復關、隴，是年五月大發秦、晉之師會汴城下，屯杏花營，諸軍環城而壘。

translations.literal: When Chaghan Temür had repeatedly broken the rebels and wholly recovered Guan and Long, in the fifth month of that year he greatly sent Qin and Jin armies to assemble below Bian city, encamped at Apricot Blossom Camp, and the hosts ringed the city with fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: After Chaghan Temür had routed the rebels repeatedly and recovered the Guanzhong and Longyou regions, he massed Qin and Jin armies before Kaifeng in the fifth month, encamped at Apricot Blossom Camp, and ringed the city with siege lines.

sentences.zh: 林兒兵出戰輒敗，嬰城守百餘日，食將盡。

translations.literal: Lin'er's troops went out to battle and were repeatedly defeated; they clung to the city in defense for more than a hundred days until provisions were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'er's men sallied and were beaten every time; they held the walls for over a hundred days until food ran low.

sentences.zh: 福通計無所出，挾林兒從百騎開東門遁還安豐，後宮官屬子女及符璽印章寶貨盡沒於察罕。

translations.literal: Futong, with no plan left, took Lin'er with a hundred horsemen, opened the east gate and fled back to Anfeng; the inner palace, officials, attendants, sons and daughters, seals, tallies, and treasures all fell to Chaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Futong, at his wits' end, fled through the east gate with Lin'er and a hundred horsemen back to Anfeng; palace women, officials, children, seals, and treasure all fell to Chaghan.

sentences.zh: 時毛貴已為其党趙均用所殺，有續繼祖者，又殺均用，所部自相攻擊。

translations.literal: At this time Mao Gui had already been killed by his partisan Zhao Junyong; one Xu Jizu then killed Junyong — their divisions attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: By then Mao Gui had been killed by his follower Zhao Junyong; Xu Jizu then killed Junyong, and their factions turned on one another.

sentences.zh: 獨田豐據東平，勢稍強。

translations.literal: Only Tian Feng held Dongping; his power was somewhat strong.
translations.idiomatic: Only Tian Feng still held Dongping, and his strength was comparatively intact.

sentences.zh: 二十年，關先生等陷大寧，復犯上都。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Master Guan and others took Daining and again struck Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Master Guan and his men seized Daining and raided Shangdu again.

sentences.zh: 田豐陷保定，元遣使招之，被殺。

translations.literal: Tian Feng took Baoding; Yuan sent envoys to summon him — he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Feng captured Baoding; when Yuan envoys came to negotiate surrender, he had them killed.

sentences.zh: 王士誠又躪晉、冀。

translations.literal: Wang Shicheng again trampled Jin and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shicheng overran Shanxi and Hebei again.

sentences.zh: 元將孛羅敗之於台州，遂入東平與豐合。

translations.literal: The Yuan general Bayan defeated him at Taizhou; he then entered Dongping and joined with Feng.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan general Bayan defeated him at Taizhou; he then withdrew into Dongping and joined Tian Feng.

sentences.zh: 福通嘗責李武、崔德逗撓，將罪之。

translations.literal: Futong once blamed Li Wu and Cui De for delay and shirking and was about to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Futong had rebuked Li Wu and Cui De for dragging their feet and was ready to punish them.

sentences.zh: 二十一年夏，兩人叛去，降于李思齊。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-first year the two rebelled and went over, surrendering to Li Sizhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twenty-first year both defected to Li Sizhi.

sentences.zh: 時李喜喜、關先生等東西轉戰，已多走死，餘黨自高麗還寇上都，孛羅復擊降之。

translations.literal: At this time Li Xixi, Master Guan and others fought east and west in rotation; many had already fled to their deaths; remnant bands returning from Goryeo raided Shangdu — Bayan again attacked and made them surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xixi, Master Guan, and others had ranged east and west until most were dead or scattered; survivors returning from Goryeo struck at Shangdu, and Bayan defeated and accepted their surrender.

sentences.zh: 而察罕既取汴梁，遂遣子擴廓討東平，脅降田豐、王士誠，乘勝定山東。

translations.literal: Chaghan, having already taken Bianliang, then sent his son Köke Temür to campaign against Dongping, coerced the surrender of Tian Feng and Wang Shicheng, and following victory settled Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chaghan held Kaifeng he sent his son Köke Temür against Dongping, forced Tian Feng and Wang Shicheng to submit, and swept Shandong while victory lasted.

sentences.zh: 惟陳猱頭者，獨守益都不下，與福通遙為聲援。

translations.literal: Only Chen the Monkey-head alone held Yidu and would not yield, giving distant mutual support with Futong.
translations.idiomatic: Only Chen the Monkey-head still held Yidu and refused to yield, coordinating with Futong from afar.

sentences.zh: 二十二年六月，豐、士誠乘閑刺殺察罕，入益都。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-second year Feng and Shicheng seized an opening to assassinate Chaghan and entered Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-second year Tian Feng and Wang Shicheng ambushed and killed Chaghan, then marched into Yidu.

sentences.zh: 元以兵柄付擴廓，圍城數重，猱頭等告急。

translations.literal: Yuan entrusted military authority to Köke Temür; he ringed the city in many layers — Monkey-head and the others sent urgent appeals.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan gave command to Köke Temür, who tightened siege upon siege; Monkey-head sent desperate appeals for help.

sentences.zh: 福通自安豐引兵赴援，遇元師于火星埠，大敗走還。

translations.literal: Futong led troops from Anfeng to relieve them; he met Yuan forces at Mars Ford, was greatly defeated and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Futong marched from Anfeng to relieve the city but met Yuan troops at Mars Ford, was routed, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 元兵急攻益都，穴地道以入，殺豐、士城，而械送猱頭于京師，林兒勢大窘。

translations.literal: Yuan troops pressed the attack on Yidu, tunneled underground to enter, killed Feng and Shicheng, and sent Monkey-head in fetters to the capital — Lin'er's power was greatly straitened.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan forces stormed Yidu, broke in through sappers' tunnels, killed Tian Feng and Wang Shicheng, and sent Monkey-head in chains to the capital; Lin'er's cause was in dire straits.

sentences.zh: 明年，張士誠將呂珍圍安豐，林兒告急于太祖。

translations.literal: The next year Zhang Shicheng's general Lü Zhen besieged Anfeng; Lin'er appealed in urgency to the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhang Shicheng's general Lü Zhen besieged Anfeng, and Lin'er begged the Founding Emperor for aid.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「安豐破則士誠益強。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor said: "If Anfeng falls, Shicheng will grow stronger still."
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor said, "If Anfeng falls, Zhang Shicheng will only grow stronger."

sentences.zh: 」遂親帥師往救，而珍已入城殺福通。

translations.literal: " He then personally led the army to rescue them — but Zhen had already entered the city and killed Futong.
translations.idiomatic: " He led the army in person, but Lü Zhen had already entered the city and killed Futong.

sentences.zh: 太祖擊走珍，以林兒歸，居之滁州。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor struck and drove off Zhen, brought Lin'er back, and settled him at Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor drove Lü Zhen off, brought Lin'er away, and housed him at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，太祖為吳王。

translations.literal: The next year the Founding Emperor became King of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Founding Emperor took the title King of Wu.

sentences.zh: 又二年，林兒卒。

translations.literal: Two years later Lin'er died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years after that Lin'er died.

sentences.zh: 或曰太祖命廖永忠迎林兒歸應天，至瓜步，覆舟沉于江雲。

translations.literal: Some say the Founding Emperor ordered Liao Yongzhong to welcome Lin'er back to Yingtian; at Guabu the boat capsized and he sank in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that the Founding Emperor sent Liao Yongzhong to escort Lin'er to Yingtian, and that at Guabu the boat overturned and he drowned in the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：元之末季，群雄蜂起。

translations.literal: The encomium says: In the late season of Yuan, numerous heroes swarmed up like bees.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: In the closing years of the Yuan, rival warlords rose everywhere.

sentences.zh: 子興據有濠州，地偏勢弱。

translations.literal: Zixing held Haozhou — the territory was remote and his strength weak.
translations.idiomatic: Zixing held only Haozhou, remote and weak in power.

sentences.zh: 然有明基業，實肇于滁陽一旅。

translations.literal: Yet the foundation of the Ming enterprise truly began from that one band at Chuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Ming enterprise itself began with that single force at Chuyang.

sentences.zh: 子興之封王祀廟，食報久長，良有以也。

translations.literal: Zixing's enfeoffment as prince, his sacrifices and temple, and the long enjoyment of recompense — all have good reason.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous enfeoffment, temple rites, and enduring reward were richly deserved.

sentences.zh: 林兒橫據中原，縱兵蹂躪，蔽遮江、淮十有餘年。

translations.literal: Lin'er sprawled across the central plains, loosed troops to trample and ravage, and screened the Yangzi and Huai for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'er dominated the central plains, letting his armies ravage the land and shielding the Yangzi–Huai region for more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 太祖得以從容締造者，藉其力焉。

translations.literal: That the Founding Emperor was able at leisure to forge his creation borrowed their strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor could build his realm at leisure in no small part because of that distraction.

sentences.zh: 帝王之興，必有先驅者資之以成其業，夫豈偶然哉！

translations.literal: When emperors and kings rise, there must be forerunners who supply resources to complete their enterprise — how could it be accidental!
translations.idiomatic: Every imperial rise has forerunners whose labor makes the triumph possible — nothing accidental about it!
